dedupe_keys.name: nchrp 08 36 43 return on investment on freight rail capacity improvement

description: NCHRP Project 08-36, Task 43, Return on Investment on Freight Rail Capacity Improvement, was prepared by David Hunt of Cambridge Systematics with Reebie Associates for the National Cooperative Highway Research Program at the request of the AASHTO Standing Committee on Planning (April 2005). It asks how to show what the public obtains from investing in rail freight capacity, since railroads own their track and invest where it is most profitable. Coverage: eleven case studies of publicly supported freight rail projects, including the Alameda Corridor, Chicago's CREATE programme, an Iowa CMAQ example, the FRA benefit-cost methodology, the Freight-Rail Bottom Line Report, the I-81 marketing analysis, the Mid-Atlantic Rail Operations Study, the New York Cross Harbor goods movement environmental impact statement, the Northern Ohio corridor, the Palouse River and Coulee City Railroad and the Shellpot Bridge; a review of travel demand, transport impact, external impact, economic impact and decision methods and software; federal and state funding programmes; and a framework for quantifying public benefits. Format and access: a report PDF on the TRB site. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: the case studies and costs date from before 2005. The framework can be used to structure the benefit side when freight network flow models compare rail capacity projects. It relates to the Freight Analysis Framework and the St. Louis intermodal hub study in the catalogue.
